chapter_title: Concerning the Twelve Signs of the Zodiac and the
spiritual_reading:
Whether the full arrangement of general governing influences in the outermost understanding, or the sufficient set of dominant impulses that move through them, all these are ruling powers, each acting from its own quality. They stand in mutual hostility and rivalry, with one pressing upon another and each threatening the rest. They take from one another through the operation of the ordering power that has brought the whole system of states into a formed sequence. That ordering power has gathered these influences, fixed them in the outermost plane, and held them within a continually recurring cycle. And as that cycle turns and drives them through their alternations, they carry out whatever their ruling loves crave, acting in both inner and outer life according to their delight. Yet over them there is a restraining oversight, a superior exaction that watches their motion, compelling them, drawing from them what is due, and taking away from them what they would claim as their own.

This is the way it can be understood in an orderly manner. Those ruling influences were seized out of a full series of fundamental evils and falsities and fixed into the outermost cycle, so that the whole could be governed as one. From each fundamental origin a paired determination was taken, so that every kind of perversion might have its representative form within the general arrangement. From the obscuring of understanding that feigns intelligence, there arose the twin power of divided reasoning and confident persuasion. From the burning of self-love there arose the power of initiating from self and the power of domineering over others. From the volatility of persuasion that disturbs discernment, there arose the power of possessive craving, the power of balancing by self-justification, and the power of casting truths into mere opinion. From the falsification of truth that should have been living, there arose the power of enclosing affection within appearances, the power of separating purity from charity, and the power of immersing the mind in fluctuating pretense. From active denial of good, there arose the power of hard restraint and the power of secret malice. These are the full set of ruling depraved tendencies, by which evil is set in motion and maintained; for they bring forth every kind of disorder in the human mind and in its effects, whether the disorder appears in perception or in act.

Understand also the leaders among these influences, those more immediate chief impulses: from where they were generated. The ruling impulse of self-derived counsel and proud reasoning arose from the obscuring of understanding. The ruling impulse of alluring delight arose from the burning of self-love. The ruling impulse of contention and assault arose from volatile persuasion. The ruling impulse of subtle calculation and shifting interpretation arose from falsified truth. The ruling impulse of cold resistance and despairing constraint arose from active denial of good.

Also, two chief determinations are counted with the burning of love and its craving: one that hardens into resistance and one that yields into appetite. These two are as a generative pair for the whole of these influences, because from the interplay of such contraries the remaining perversions gain their power to multiply and to act.

Also, governing lights were numbered among them as a rule, so that the whole arrangement might be held under a superior ordering in its ongoing operation. It can be seen that these higher governing principles continually subjugate the depraved influences, checking them at every moment and forcing them to serve within bounds.

These seven that have been named—the sufficient set of chief impulses together with the two generative determinations—are the operative powers of evil that bring about every disorderly act in the whole scope of life, in inward intention and outward behavior, in every form of affection and thought, in the resistance of what is closed and the flow of what is receptive, in perception and in deed.

Again, these general governing influences are arranged into a complete distribution: they are appointed to the full compass of the outermost plane, three to each quarter, so that every ultimate condition may be encompassed. They are fixed within the recurring cycle of external life. The group that springs from self-initiating pride, domineering ambition, and confident persuasion stands together as one quarter. The group that springs from possessive craving, hard restraint, and the separation of purity from charity stands together as another quarter. The group that springs from divided reasoning, self-justifying balance, and casting truths into mere opinion stands together as another quarter. The group that springs from secret malice, fluctuating pretense, and enclosing affection within appearances stands together as the remaining quarter. Thus they are set in fourfold completeness, distributed through the outermost cycle.

Therefore, when the quarter driven by self-initiating pride, domineering ambition, and confident persuasion is forcibly exacted and stripped by the restraining oversight that is over it, together with the chief impulses that operate there, then immediately disorder strikes the lower affections that belong to the natural mind. But when the quarter driven by possessive craving, the separation of purity from charity, and hard restraint is forcibly exacted, then at once disorder befalls the elementary perceptions and their derivative knowledges, together with all the uses and works that proceed from them. Again, when the quarter driven by secret malice, fluctuating pretense, and enclosing affection within appearances is forcibly exacted, then there is a lack of living truth in the outer life, and a drying up of understanding from one state to another. Conversely, when the quarter driven by divided reasoning, self-justifying balance, and casting truths into mere opinion is forcibly exacted, then distortion and diminishment befall the form of human thought and will as it is expressed in life, varying from one state to another.

Behold, it has now been made plain concerning the full set of general governing depraved influences: they were formed out of the series of fundamental evils and falsities and fixed into the outermost cycle.

It has also been taught concerning the other five chief impulses: they too arose from those same fundamental origins of denial and perversion.

And it has been recounted concerning the two generative determinations: they belong to the hidden activity of burning love turned into craving, in the resistant mode and in the yielding mode, acting as a generative pair.

And again it has been disclosed concerning the higher governing lights: they are not of the same kind as these depraved influences. Yet, because the outermost plane must be held in order by what governs and because whatever is present in that plane receives determination from higher influx, they were numbered together in the external reckoning, since the depraved influences are compelled to be checked and stripped within that arrangement. For these higher governing principles are from a superior source of life and order, not arising from the depraved impulses or from the general governing perversions of the outermost cycle.

fills.notes: The passage is defining the twelve as the fixed representatives of the five dark roots, i.e., stable governing perversions. Correspondentially they are what keeps disorder in motion and in form; thus “wickedness shall not cease” (not “be destroyed” or “be judged,” which would shift into later moral or soteriological register).

The clause needs the universal effect of these rulers in ultimates. In the substrate register this is not moral exhortation but structural consequence: they are causes of “evil and disorder in the world,” appearing in both vegetative and animate planes (tree and flesh).

assessment: Most lacunae are trivial letter-restorations fixed by the preserved surrounding wording. The two substantive gaps in ¶3 are tightly constrained by the correspondential structure: (a) the twelve rulers are stable ultimates taken from the five dark roots, so wickedness is said not to cease; (b) their effect is universal disorder manifested in both vegetative and animate realms, requiring a generic term like “disorder in the world” rather than later moralizing or salvific phrasing.
